title.value: When Do We Need Graph Neural Networks for Node Classification?
title.justification: The title is the main focus of the paper, which aims to identify when graph neural networks (GNNs) should be used for node classification tasks.
title.quote: When Do We Need Graph Neural Networks for Node Classification?

extractions.description: This paper investigates the conditions under which Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) outperform traditional Neural Networks (NNs) in node classification tasks. Using graph signal processing and statistical hypothesis testing, the authors propose two measures, Normalized Total Variation (NTV) and Normalized Smoothness Value (NSV), to evaluate the impact of edge biases on feature and label performance on graphs. The study aims to predict when GNNs have performance advantages over graph-agnostic models like Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) on non-trivial graph datasets by conducting statistical analysis based on these measures.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the theoretical and methodological aspects of Graph Neural Networks for node classification and does not specifically address any eco-responsible applications or sectors.
primary_category.quote: Though GNNs are believed to outperform basic NNs in real-world tasks, it is found that in some cases, GNNs have little performance gain or even underperform graph-agnostic NNs.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not target any specific eco-responsible sub-category as it concentrates on the methodological aspect of node classification using GNNs rather than environmental applications.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we explore an explanation and propose two proper measures to determine when to use GNNs for a node classification task.

new_primary_category.justification: The focus of this paper is on methodological advancements rather than direct applications in eco-responsible categories, hence there is no need for a new category.
new_primary_category.quote: In some cases, even a simple Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) can outperform GNNs by a large margin... This makes us wonder when it is appropriate to use GNNs.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new eco-responsible sub-category is required as the paper is primarily concerned with the technical analysis of GNNs' performance, which doesn't align with the eco-responsible AI framework.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: ...propose two measures which analyze the cases in which the edge bias in features and labels does not provide advantages.
